intent: Show, per session, how many API round-trips were spent on work that decided nothing, so the waste can be scripted away instead of guessed at.
scope: Non-goal: acting on the findings, or changing existing detector scoring
changes: turns.py classifies a Bash command as poll / lint_test / vcs_check / substantive. Deliberately conservative: state-changing commands (git commit, git push) are substantive even though they are scriptable, and a turn is mechanical only when every command in it is — so the reported waste is a floor, not a guess.
parse.py groups tool calls by requestId rather than by transcript line. One API response can span several lines, and per-line counting reported 0% batching where the true rate is 12%.
records.py adds TurnEfficiency (schema v3, additive: pre-v3 records read as zeros) with derived batching/mechanical rates written into to_dict so consumers need not recompute them.
report.py adds a Turn efficiency section pricing each mechanical kind at the measured average context re-read per turn.

Turn state and totals were folded into a _TurnTracker class after pylint flagged _Accumulator at 15/12 instance attributes. The budget allowed exactly one new attribute, which forced the right shape: the open turn exists only to be folded into the totals, so they belong in one object. _Accumulator.turns is now a property, keeping every existing caller and test unchanged.

verification.evidence: 112 passed; every module in the package at 100% statement and branch coverage, including the new turns.py (25 stmts / 12 branches).

verification.command: ruff check && ruff format --check && pylint && mypy
verification.evidence: ruff: All checks passed, formatted. pylint 10.00/10. mypy clean. 112 tests, every module at 100% statement and branch coverage.

263 transcripts analyzed in 1.8s. Report: 33,508 tool turns carrying 37,411 calls, batched 2,595 (8%), avg context re-read 606k/turn; mechanical 4,437 turns (13%) ~= 2.7B cache-read tokens (poll 891, lint/test 2,044, vcs 1,502).

risks: The classifier is regex-based, so an unusual command shape can be misfiled. Mitigated by the conservative rule (mixed turns count as substantive), which biases the number down rather than up.

Grouping by requestId depends on that field being present; lines without one fall back to the message id, and turns with neither collapse together. Only affects batching precision, not the mechanical counts.
Schema v3 records are read by older code as unknown keys, which record_from_dict already ignores; no migration is needed.
rollback: git revert the commit; TurnEfficiency is additive so stored v3 records remain readable by the reverted code, which ignores the extra key.
Re-run scan --force && report and confirm REPORT.md renders without the Turn efficiency section.
